title: Wrong-way driver kills 30yo, tells police “sorry bro”
description:
Note: If you are a family member of this victim, please reach out and let us know how we can be supporting you during this time. 
Sincerely, 
The volunteers at MN Safety

Incident data per Minnesota State Patrol:

Incident type:Fatal
CR:22502267
Date/Time:02/18/2022 03:58
 
District:2500 West Metro
 
Location: East 394 at Plymouth, MINNETONKA, Hennepin County
 
Description:The Jeep Wrangler entered wrong way onto the Eastbound Lanes of Interstate 394 from 6th street, in downtown Minneapolis. The Jeep continued West and struck the Chrysler Sebring that was traveling Eastbound, head on at Plymouth Road.
 
 
Road Condition:Dry
 
Outside agencies: Minnetonka Police Department, Minnetonka Fire Department, HCMC Ambulance, North Ambulance

Information believed complete
Last updated:02/18/2022 05:52

2 Vehicles involved.
Vehicle
2006 Chrysler Sebring

Melrose, MN, USA

transcript.text: i394 coming from downtown minneapolis we've got a wrong way driver that is first reported by local news anchor jason derusha who said he had his own very close call with the vehicle police working urgently to catch up to this 2020 jeep wrangler with no tail lights unfortunately this did result in a deadly crash we'll give you a warning before we get to that part which is at the end of the video. But police are following alongside the vehicle and put a spotlight on it to try to enhance visibility for oncoming drivers. Our policy is to generally not publish fatal crashes unless they involve particularly egregious driver conduct or considerable news. This qualifies in both areas. There was considerable local coverage of this. And of course, driving the wrong way on the freeway, possibly drunk, clearly egregious, egregious driver behavior. And seeing, real-world videos like this might help us all become more aware and informed drivers ourselves again you can see those taillights off traveling at freeway speeds thankfully that car was able to get out of the way there at the last minute but not a particularly easy-to-see vehicle even with the police following along with that spotlight we've posted several videos of wrong-way drivers on Minnesota highways and have a dedicated playlist at the end of this video so you can see for yourself what these drivers are really like. And recently we posted video of a state trooper trying to stop a wrong way driver by bumping them and some people apparently thought the officer was out of line. So this is a video which shows what happens if you just can't quite stop a wrong way driver in time. We were going to do analysis of the force and vehicles involved and indeed the larger mass of the Jeep played a role against a smaller car. And also the car was older and received a marginal safety rating. from the I-IHS and the Jeep is much newer and has good safety ratings across the board. But maybe the bigger story here is the basic facts. A 20-year-old, not even old enough to drink legally, is suspected of drunk driving, ignoring police, causing a deadly crash, and then, when confronted about the death, he allegedly told the troopers, sorry bro. The 20-year-old suspect with an address out of St. Anthony was then able to post a $150,000 bond and has retained a private attorney. Looking at the video in front of you, you can see one squad car staying with the vehicle, lighting it up, and a second squad working to quickly overtake them. Now a warning, the crash video will start shortly. We try to post safety video and facts and let you draw your own conclusions. A quick thank you to Paul Bloom and the Fox 9 team, which was first to note, the 20-year-old suspect posting $150,000 bond, and allegedly admitting he had 10,000. drinks and apparently blew a .2 BAC and it was WCCO's Jason Derusha who first broke news of the crash and captured some of the photos the original source for these traffic camera videos is the Minnesota Department of Transportation and in safety this YouTube channel is not associated with any governmental agency we're just volunteers trying to promote public safety and education

event_summary.short: Wrong-way driver causes fatal head-on crash on I-394 in Minnetonka, killing 30-year-old male; suspect allegedly told police 'sorry bro'.
